The company entered a first amendment to its HaloMD dispute-resolution services agreement. Fees move to a pay-on-collected basis, the term is extended, and the company expects lower arbitration costs. The Fifth Circuit, sitting en banc, upheld vacatur of key No Surprises Act rule provisions on ghost rates and on excluding bonus and incentive payments from the qualifying payment amount (QPA). The company reported this in an 8-K.

business_model.claim: Nutex is a physician-led healthcare services company. Its hospital division runs micro-hospitals, specialty hospitals and hospital outpatient departments, and it also has a population health management division. As of September 30, 2026 it had 28 hospital facilities in 12 states.
quotes: Nutex Health Inc. is a physician-led, healthcare services and operations company with 28 hospital facilities in 12 states (hospital division), and a primary care-centric, risk-bearing population health management division.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the 'almost all' wording is inferred from the revenue split
business_model.claim: The company reports hospital, population health management (PHM) and real estate segments. The hospital division supplies almost all revenue. For the nine months to September 30, 2026, total revenue was 644,850, of which hospital was 618,519 and PHM was 26,331 (table in thousands). The real estate division's revenue is not shown separately in the evidence.
quotes: We report the results of our operations as three segments: (i) the hospital division, (ii) the PHM division, and (iii) the real estate division.

business_model.claim: Hospitals sell emergency, inpatient, behavioral health and ancillary services (imaging, lab, pharmacy). Payment comes almost entirely from insurers and other third parties, not patients, and the company is generally out-of-network, so it has no negotiated rates with most insurers. Insurance was 97% of the transaction-price allocation.
quotes: We generally operate as an out-of-network provider and as such, do not have negotiated reimbursement rates with insurance companies.
On average, greater than 99% of our net patient service revenue is paid by insurers, federal agencies and other non-patient third parties.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the mechanism is inferred from the P4 description of the IDR process
business_model.claim: A key revenue driver is the No Surprises Act independent dispute resolution (IDR) process. Management says 50-60% of billable visits go through IDR and 40-50% result in an award. When an award is made the company has prevailed in over 80% of determinations and collects over 80% of the award amounts on average.
quotes: When an award determination is made, Nutex Health prevailed in over 80% of those determinations over the last nine months and collects, on average, over 80% of the award amounts as calculated on awards from inception through March of 2026.

business_model.claim: Reported revenue depends heavily on management's estimates of variable consideration on arbitrated claims. In 2024 a change in estimate added about $169.7 million to revenue and about $112.0 million to pre-tax income.
quotes: This change in estimate increased revenue and net income before tax for the year ended December 31, 2024 by approximately $169.7 million and $112.0 million, respectively.

business_model.claim: Revenue fell in 2026 even though visit volume grew. Q3 2026 revenue was 217,613 against 267,804 a year earlier (table in thousands), down 18.7%, while hospital visits rose 18.1% to 54,622. Management attributes the decline mainly to 2025 revenue having been lifted by higher estimates for 2024 services and by ineligible charts later reconciled.
quotes: The decrease was primarily driven by factors that favorably impacted revenue recognized in 2025, including the availability of additional collection data that supported higher estimates for services rendered in 2024, and the reconciliation of certain ineligible charts during the fourth quarter of 2025 that had been included from mid-2024 through the first nine months of 2025.

risks.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6) and income statement (F2); the persistence of the decline is inferred.
risks.claim: Revenue fell sharply in the latest quarter and the nine months, with same-hospital hospital revenue down more than total revenue. This suggests the 2025 revenue base was inflated by favorable estimates.
quotes: Total revenue decreased 18.7% to $217.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $267.8 million for the same period in 2025, while hospital division revenue at same hospitals decreased 20.1%.

risks.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6) and cash flow statement (F3); the effect on underlying profit is inferred.
risks.claim: Nine-month 2026 profit includes a $52.3 million non-cash reduction to contract services expense from a change in estimate, which flatters comparisons and may not recur.
quotes: Results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 include a $52.3 million reduction to contract services expense resulting from a change in estimate related to the June 30, 2026 amendment to the Company’s agreement with HaloMD and the reduction in the CMS administrative fee, which increased net income attributable to Nutex Health by $25.0 million, or $4.83 per diluted share.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors (P2), the 10-Q (P4) and the 8-K (P10); the severity of a rupture is inferred.
risks.claim: The company depends on a single exclusive vendor, HaloMD, for its arbitration claims. The company has no audit access to the vendor's work, and the vendor faces insurer lawsuits.
quotes: Nutex has no contractual right to access or audit HaloMD’s proprietary benchmarking data or documents prepared and submitted by HaloMD to the IDREs on behalf of the Company, such as petitions, position statements, methodology formulas, payment demand letters and arbitration briefs.

risks.basis: Stated in the 8-Ks (P7, P8) and the 10-Q risk factors (P5); the eventual cost is not stated.
risks.claim: A cybersecurity incident involving exfiltration and publication of patient, employee and business data has led to several putative class actions, and its financial impact is not yet quantified.
quotes: At this stage, the Company is unable to predict the outcome of the litigation or estimate the potential impact of the incident on the Company’s business strategy, operations, financial condition, results of operations or the trading price of the Company’s common stock.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-Q (P4) and balance sheet (F1); the effect on collections is inferred.
risks.claim: Enforcement of unpaid IDR awards is legally unsettled, which is a collection risk on a large receivables balance.
quotes: In September 2026, aligning with the Fifth Circuit, the Second Circuit also held that the NSA does not provide an implied private right of action for providers to enforce IDR payment awards.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors (P2); the latest figures are in the 10-Q (F2, F3).
risks.claim: Earn-out share obligations to former doctor owners of under-construction hospitals may dilute existing holders, and some former owners dispute how the share count is calculated.
quotes: The aggregate number of additional shares we may be required to issue could significantly dilute the voting power of our existing stockholders.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the earnings release; the run-rate question is inferred from the revenue and visit trends
unresolved_questions.claim: Third-quarter total revenue fell 18.7% to $217.6 million from $267.8 million, while visits rose. Is the lower revenue a one-time reset of 2025 estimates, or a lower run-rate for IDR-driven revenue?
quotes: The decrease was primarily driven by factors that favorably impacted revenue recognized in 2025, including the availability of additional collection data that supported higher estimates for services rendered in 2024, and the reconciliation of certain ineligible charts during the fourth quarter of 2025 that had been included from mid-2024 through the first nine months of 2025.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated amounts in the release and 8-K; the split between one-time and recurring effect is not given
unresolved_questions.claim: Nine-month results include a $52.3 million non-cash reduction to contract services expense, worth $25.0 million to net income attributable to Nutex. How much of this is retroactive catch-up and how much recurs as lower ongoing arbitration costs?
quotes: Results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 include a $52.3 million reduction to contract services expense resulting from a change in estimate related to the June 30, 2026 amendment to the Company’s agreement with HaloMD and the reduction in the CMS administrative fee, which increased net income attributable to Nutex Health by $25.0 million, or $4.83 per diluted share.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the 8-Ks and 10-Q; the eventual impact is unknown
unresolved_questions.claim: What is the financial, legal and regulatory cost of the August 2026 cyber incident, in which data was exfiltrated and later published by the unauthorized third party?
quotes: At this stage, the Company is unable to predict the outcome of the litigation or estimate the potential impact of the incident on the Company’s business strategy, operations, financial condition, results of operations or the trading price of the Company’s common stock.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated that all dismissals are appealed; the outcome is not known
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the appeals of the dismissed insurer lawsuits against IDR vendors such as HaloMD and providers change how IDR awards are treated, and could they affect Nutex's awards and collections?
quotes: All dismissed cases have been appealed.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the 10-Q; legislative odds are not addressed in the evidence
unresolved_questions.claim: Would the proposed Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act replace IDR with an insurer-set rate, and how likely is it to advance, given Nutex's out-of-network IDR-based model?
quotes: Rep. Frank Pallone’s Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act, introduced on October 8, 2026, would instead eliminate IDR entirely for services furnished on or after January 1, 2028.

unresolved_questions.basis: ruling stated in the 8-K; the revenue effect is inferred and unquantified
unresolved_questions.claim: Does the Fifth Circuit en banc ruling on ghost rates and incentive payments raise QPAs and IDR awards, and will it show up in Nutex's collections?
quotes: A majority of the en banc court ruled that insurers may not include so-called “ghost rates” in their QPA calculations and must include bonus and incentive payments.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from conflicting captions across the cited items and the stated dispute
unresolved_questions.claim: What are the current share count and the remaining earn-out dilution? The XBRL balance sheet caption shows 6,951,622 and 5,511,452 shares, the earnings release shows 6,857,504 and 7,086,670 shares at the Sept. 30, 2026 and Dec. 31, 2025 dates, and some former hospital owners dispute the number of earn-out shares owed.
quotes: 6,951,622 and 5,511,452 shares issued and outstanding as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively
6,857,504 and 7,086,670 shares issued and outstanding as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively

Former owners of certain under construction hospitals have disputed the number of additional shares issuable to them in accordance with the formula agreed upon at the time of the merger (as described above) and assert, among other things, that the number of shares in the calculation should not be adjusted for the 2024 Reverse Stock Splits.

unresolved_questions.basis: cash-flow amounts are stated; the program terms are not in the packet
unresolved_questions.claim: Cash used for stock repurchases and retirements was 50,689 (table in thousands) in the first nine months of 2026, against $5.0 million for all of 2025. What program authorizes these purchases, and will they continue?
quotes: Cash related to stock repurchases and retirements was $5.0 million.

unresolved_questions.basis: receivable figures are stated; the cause of the rise is not given and is inferred only as a question

quotes: collects, on average, over 80% of the award amounts as calculated on awards from inception through March of 2026

unresolved_questions.basis: stated differing counts in the cited items; the reasons for the differences are not given
unresolved_questions.claim: How many new hospitals will open in 2026 and what do they cost? The 10-K gave four, the MD&A in the same 10-K gave three, and the Q3 release cites two expected in the fourth quarter.
quotes: We expect to open four new hospital facilities in 2026.
We expect to open three new hospital facilities by the end of 2026.
with the expected opening of two new hospitals in the fourth quarter

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from the printed quarterly and nine-month figures; the cause is not stated

quotes: Total stock-based compensation expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.4 million, compared to $119.6 million for the same period in 2025.
